### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **42** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7da99b79f5fcf3fa1dfc143f39d73fb702dfb271`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `resolveExecCtx (34 routes)`, `routeManager (23 routes)`, `resolveRequestEnvironmentId (4 routes)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7da99b79f5fcf3fa1dfc143f39d73fb702dfb271` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5f552fc5951bf2322833ea08f9b87d053ee2e045` — the merge of head `12af728fa8a19542811c866268a2bbb27cd105c4` into base `7da99b79f5fcf3fa1dfc143f39d73fb702dfb271`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5f552fc5951bf2322833ea08f9b87d053ee2e045 && git checkout 5f552fc5951bf2322833ea08f9b87d053ee2e045
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7da99b79f5fcf3fa1dfc143f39d73fb702dfb271 12af728fa8a19542811c866268a2bbb27cd105c4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7da99b79f5fcf3fa1dfc143f39d73fb702dfb271 && git merge --no-ff 12af728fa8a19542811c866268a2bbb27cd105c4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7da99b79f5fcf3fa1dfc143f39d73fb702dfb271
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7da99b79f5fcf3fa1dfc143f39d73fb702dfb271` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `12af728fa8a19542811c866268a2bbb27cd105c4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/spec/src/api/rest-server.zod.ts` + `content/docs/references/api/rest-server.mdx` (the row `gen:docs` renders from that describe), `packages/rest/src/meta-record-currency-backfill-route.ts` and `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` (the mount the sentence now names), `packages/rest/src/rest-config-mount-table.pin.test.ts` (the pin that holds the switch to four routes), `.changeset/30675-record-currency-backfill-rest-door.md` (the `@objectstack/spec` patch the consent requires). The rest of the diff is read here too at the lane's own tier (card #30675, ruling 6670707546 item B); the ACCEPT names it.

Read: card #30675 (body, all 7 comments: claim 6675312689, amendments 6675340866 and 6675450053, dev report 6677009085), ruling 6670707546 item B, A card #30674 and its ACCEPT 6673657336, domain:spec#2's consent 6675431663, the PR body, and `git diff 561d532c4..12af728fa` (merge-base of `origin/main` and the head: 29 files, +1031/−18, the API file list and the local diff agree). Check-runs read through the API at 2026-11-06T04:51Z; nothing built, run or re-run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

**Shape.** `POST {metaPath}/_migrate-record-currency-codes` in a new module `meta-record-currency-backfill-route.ts`, registered from `registerMetadataEndpointsInner` (head L5608–5621) beside the object state read, inside the umbrella's route-manager swap, so it sits under the `/meta` anonymous-deny gate as `_migrate-stored` does. Body `{ object, field, code, apply? }`, closed; the answer is `backfillRecordCurrencyCodes`' report as `data` of the shared envelope. Right.

- **Same switch as `_migrate-stored`.** Yes. The registrar returns on `metadata.endpoints.maintenance === false` (route L983); `_migrate-stored` registers under `metadata.endpoints.maintenance !== false` (`meta-collection-routes.ts` L315 on `main`). The two spellings agree for a boolean with default `true`. The mount-table pin now holds the switch to exactly four routes (`_drafts`, `diagnostics`, `_migrate-record-currency-codes`, `_migrate-stored`), and the route test pins the sibling switches leave it mounted and the scoped base mounts its twin.
- **Tenant-admin authorized.** Yes, as the card fixed it: `setup.write` in `ctx.systemPermissions`, `isSystem` bypassing (route L991–998), asked first, before the body and before the engine, the `_migrate-stored` order. `systemPermissions` come from `resolveUserAuthzGrants(ql, userId, { tenantId })`, so the capability is the one the caller holds in its current organization. `manage_metadata` alone and `setup.access` alone are refused 403 (route test; the write-door enumeration's new `DATA_DOORS` cases on both bases). The `isSystem` bypass is now owned by row 50b of `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`, with the regenerated register row. The card left `manage_metadata` as the alternative only if the maintainer names it; nobody has.
- **Scoped to the caller's organization; the unscoped run refused before any write.** Yes. `organizationId` is `ctx.tenantId` and nothing else (route L1000); the body may not carry `organizationId` or `allOrganizations` (each is 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` with its own sentence, L954–956), so no environment-wide form exists on this surface. `ctx.tenantId` is the session's `activeOrganizationId` (or the API key's), vetted by `vetOrganizationClaim` against `accessible_org_ids` and dropped when the claim fails (`resolve-authz-context.ts` L624, L779–790 on `main`). A context with no organization, `isSystem` included, is 403 before any read (L1001–1009; pinned with the provider never called and zero driver reads). The CLI's refusal of the unscoped multi-organization run therefore has no counterpart to reach: every call is the `--org` run for one organization, and the test holds that every driver read of the rows carries `"organization_id":"org_a"` and that B's admin writes `b1` and nothing of A's. The backfill itself runs `{ isSystem: true, tenantId: organizationId }` on the walk and the writes, unchanged from the A card.
- **`localization.currency` read only where D8 allows.** It is not read at all. The diff contains no occurrence of `localization`; the backfill's three mentions on the head are the comments that forbid it (ADR-0144 D8 rule 4, the code is never derived). The SDK docblock says `code` is the one you give, never derived.
- **The truncated preview says it is truncated.** Yes, carried item 2. The JSON report already carried `truncated`; the shared text no longer prints the "✓ Every … nothing to backfill" line for a capped walk (`record-currency-backfill.ts` L466–473), says "Walk incomplete", and an unscoped capped run adds that its organization check saw only the rows examined. The CLI prints the warning; REST answers the same report. Pinned in objectql and in the CLI test. Over REST the preview is the JSON report, whose `truncated` field is documented on the SDK method and in `cli.mdx`.
- **Report types re-exported.** Yes, carried item 1: `RecordCurrencyBackfillOrganization` and `RecordCurrencyBackfillOrganizationsRefusal` on the `@objectstack/objectql` entry, beside the three already there. Type-only, no runtime surface.
- **The objectql hook-refusal fix.** In scope and correct. The new door joins the `rest-write-route-hook-refusal-sentence.ledger.test.ts` population automatically (every write row of `REST_ROUTE_LEDGER`), so it had to answer the hook's sentence per row; the backfill's failure entry carried the raw `err.message`, which for a sandboxed hook is the `hook NAME threw:` debug wrapper. `rowFailureSentence` (private, not exported) reads the throw as `toFailedResult` in core's import runner does: a sandbox origin or own fault whose `mapDataError` verdict is 500 or above takes the door's withheld sentence, a sandboxed refusal takes `sandboxBusinessMessage`, and anything else keeps its message (the CONTROL test). The operator's `logger.warn` line keeps the whole text. The CLI's `--json` report reads the same sentence now, which the dev declared. No new export, no new wire code, no widened surface. The ablation (replace with `message`, rebuild, 12 ledger rows red; restore, 625 green) is the right proof and is reported with its counts.
- **Envelope and error codes.** The dev's two declared deviations hold: `sendOk` / `sendError` / `sendServerFault` for a module born today (`check:route-envelope` wants the shared pair on new modules), so the report is `data` and refusals are nested; and the SDK method returns `unknown`, not `any` (the shrink-only `exported-any-returns.json`), pinned in `return-type-precision.test.ts`. Both are improvements on the `_migrate-stored` precedent, not drifts from the card. Codes used: `FORBIDDEN`, `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, `INVALID_FIELD`, `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`, all in the registry. A declared 4xx from the body judge or the backfill is answered at its own status and code with `details.fields` when a `field` is named; anything else goes through `sendServerFault` with the route's generic text.
- **Engine access.** `wiredEngineOrLoud` plus a guarded dynamic `import('@objectstack/objectql')`, the `meta-object-state-routes.ts` precedent, with the `optional-runtime-probe` LEDGER row amendment 6675450053 admitted. No engine or no function is 501. `objectQLProvider` consumer census 6 → 7, all through the seam. The route reads no `req.query`, so rule 5's closed set does not apply (nor does `_migrate-stored` read one).
- **Remedy text.** The 409 `currency_mode_to_record` finding now names the route and its body beside the CLI command; the objectql protocol test pins both.
- **Writes carry no actor.** `modified_by` is not the admin's id, as the CLI's writes are; the PR body says so. Acceptable for a twin of the CLI; noted, not a finding.

**Observed, not blocking.**
- A non-sandboxed row failure keeps the driver's raw message in `failures[].error`, which a `setup.write` holder now reads over REST; the import row passes the same text through `sanitizeRowError`, which `@objectstack/core` does not export. The dev noted it (class c, not filed). See ③.
- The `REST_ROUTE_LEDGER` row carries no `authz` field because no conformance cell covers the door yet; the gate is held by the route test and the enumeration test instead. Fine for landing; a conformance cell is follow-up material.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: a new route, a new SDK method, two new type exports on the objectql entry, a wider `maintenance` describe. No consumer loses anything. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no authorable key, value, default or meaning changes; the `maintenance` describe is a server-config doc string, not an authoring surface. `none` takes `patch`, and the changeset gives `patch` to the six packages the diff moves: `rest`, `client`, `objectql`, `cli` (the incomplete-walk warning), `metadata-protocol` (the remedy text) and `spec` (the describe), with both declaration lines in the body matching the PR body. No `(narrowing)` arm, no BREAKING banner owed, no ADR-0087 marker owed.

**The spec hunk against consent 6675431663, line by line.** One file under `packages/spec/src`: `api/rest-server.zod.ts`, L538–541. The only change is inside the one `describe()` string of `maintenance`: the old tail "`GET /meta/_drafts` and the `POST /meta/_migrate-stored` write door" becomes "`GET /meta/_drafts`, the `POST /meta/_migrate-stored` write door and the `POST /meta/_migrate-record-currency-codes` record-currency code backfill", the sentence's own list shape with a serial "and". No key, shape, default or export changes; `lazySchema`, `z.boolean().default(true)` untouched. The mount is real in the same PR. `content/docs/references/api/rest-server.mdx` L228 changes by exactly that row, byte-equal to the concatenated describe (the shape `gen:docs` renders); no other reference page moves. The changeset carries `'@objectstack/spec': patch`. `check:generated` on the head is in the still-running `TypeScript Type Check` lanes (see counts). The terms are met; no `domain:spec` review is owed, and this record covers the hunk.

**File surface against the claim and its amendments.** Inside: `packages/rest/**` (14 files), the SDK method and its tests (3 files under `packages/client/src`), the objectql barrel, the remedy text (`protocol-write-face.ts`) and its objectql test, `content/docs/**` (4 files, `references/api/rest-server.mdx` by consent), one root changeset, `scripts/check-undeclared-dep-imports.mjs` (amendment 6675450053, one LEDGER row), `packages/spec/src/api/rest-server.zod.ts` (consent 6675431663). Beyond the named surface: `packages/objectql/src/record-currency-backfill.ts` and its test (the carried truncation item plus `rowFailureSentence`, the latter declared as a deviation), and `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/record-currency-codes.ts` and its test (+21 lines, the incomplete-walk warning, part of the carried truncation item but not named as a surface deviation in the dev report). Nothing governed; `ui/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `skills/**`, `.claude/**` untouched. Not a fork PR. 1,049 changed lines, under the 3,000 line class.

**Check-runs on the head at 2026-11-06T04:51Z:** 46 runs: 25 completed (15 success, 9 skipped, 1 failure), 21 in progress, 0 queued. Of the ten required contexts, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is success; `Test Core` (8 shards), `Build Core`, `Live E2E UI` and the `TypeScript Type Check` / `Lint & Repo Gates` lanes are still running; `Check Changeset` concluded success on this reading. The one failure is `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)`: `check:closing-target-claim` reads the governing `Claim:` 6675312689, whose `Branch:` line still names the placeholder `claude/issue-30675-record-currency-backfill-rest`; the amendment 6675340866 names `claude/project-thread-1lyw0v` but is not a `Claim:`-first-line comment, which is the only shape that guard reads. Not a finding against the diff; a seat act (below).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Raw driver text in a per-row failure over REST.** `failures[].error` keeps `err.message` for a non-sandboxed throw, so a driver's own text (SQL, table or column names) can reach a tenant admin holding `setup.write`; the import row sanitizes the same class through `sanitizeRowError`, which core does not export. Fixing it in this PR widens `@objectstack/core`'s surface, outside the claim. Recommendation: file it as a card (the card names its evidence: the import row's rule and this door), not a rider here. No maintainer ruling needed; the seat decides whether to file at ACCEPT.
- **Prose for the seat, no ruling.** (a) The PR body's Acceptance notes still call the spec describe hunk "pending spec consent … held back"; consent 6675431663 was given at 2026-11-06T02:43Z and the hunk is pushed as the head commit 12af728f. The ACCEPT should say so and quote the consent id, and the body line should be corrected through the relay. (b) The dev's open question on the assignee is moot: the PR carries `os-elon-musk` as assignee now. (c) `check:closing-target-claim` stays red until a comment whose first line begins `Claim:` and whose `Branch:` line names `claude/project-thread-1lyw0v` is posted on #30675 by this seat (remedy 1 in the guard's text; the job re-reads the thread live, no push needed). (d) The CLI edits are part of the carried truncation item; the ACCEPT should name them as an accepted surface deviation, since the dev report's deviations list does not.
- **Nothing here needs a maintainer ruling.** The gate capability is the card's own choice (`setup.write`, the ruling's recommendation); `manage_metadata` remains the alternative only if the maintainer names it on the card.
